card werk-remove  [decided]
A card can be removed, not only rewritten
why: A map with a few wrong cards is not a broken map. Cleaning up one card must not mean rewriting it into something else.

Removal is reversible and additive. `werk remove <id>` appends a `node.removed` event; `fold.ts` hides the node and its edges. Nothing leaves the log. `werk restore <id>` brings it back, and `werk removed` lists what is out.

A removed card is gone from the tree, not struck through in place. Struck-through text keeps the noise it was meant to clear.

The control sits in the card view, next to ⌖ and ▦, for the same reason accept has a button (#al-diff-cli-btn): cleanup happens while reading the map, and the judgement is already made by the time the card is on screen. The CLI verb exists too, because the agent needs a way to propose a removal.

An agent never removes a card directly. It proposes the removal and the card shows it pending, like any other change.

Children: `remove` takes the refines subtree with it. `--reparent` keeps the children and attaches them to the grandparent instead, for a bad parent over good children.

Two events, `node.removed` and `node.restored`. fold.ts applies them after the event loop and drops the node with every edge touching it, so nothing downstream learns a new concept: a removed card makes nothing stale, counts in no rollup, and cites nothing.

Removal takes the options and the excerpts of what it removes, not only the refines subtree. An option node sits nowhere in the tree, so one left behind is an orphan no view can reach and no later cleanup can find. A source two cards cite stays while either of them stays.

`--reparent` is a CLI flag with no button. The ✕ asks once, naming how many cards go with it, and that is the whole confirmation: nothing leaves the log, so the cost of a wrong click is one restore.
